comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current EWI 2026–2027 OER Article 14A (2024-and-later ordinary Applied Mathematics examination programme) and Article 15 were freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. They control over generic webpage summaries and the public programme-facts API, which does not establish the full course table. The ordinary degree has twelve first-year 5-EC positions (60), ten second-year required 5-EC units plus two elective units (60), and a 30-EC minor, three 5-EC electives and TW3-01 Bachelor Project 15 EC in year three (60). Proof Techniques combines formal TW1-11T theory 3 EC and TW1-11P practical 2 EC, counted once as 5; TW1-11T/P is not asserted as a catalogue code. Exactly one of the five electives must be non-mathematical. The neutral selection is the first four distinct mathematical table entries TW-E01 Advanced Statistics, TW-E02 Machine Learning, TW-E03 Markov Processes and TW-E04 Graph Theory, plus the first non-mathematical entry TW-E99 Algorithm Design, all 5 EC. E01 is represented in year-two Q3 and E99 in year-two Q4; E02/E03/E04 are represented in year-three Q3, and the project can use its formal Q4 period. This follows published teaching periods without certifying future timeslots or timetable compatibility. Students must consider required prior knowledge; Article 15 grants unconditional access to other TW units. Project entry requires all first-year courses and at least 40 major EC from years two and three, with topic-specific essential foundations subject to the programme director. The genuine 30-EC minor must meet approval and non-overlap rules and cannot duplicate the five electives. No double-bachelor requirements or second set of alternatives is added.
